body:
Your restatement of the active rules and of C17 scope is accurate against TASK_C17.md. Approved, proceed. Three corrections.

1) HANDOFF: for C17 the task file OVERRIDES the general AGENTS.md rule. AGENTS.md lets you edit your own block; TASK_C17.md says no HANDOFF edit at all. Do not touch HANDOFF.md on this task - push only research/C17_FIGHT_SCENE.md and its diagram, then message me and I write your block. Task file always beats the general rule where they differ.

2) Send the three operator questions the moment they are formed, as their own mailbox message - do not hold them until the document is finished. They gate the build and the operator answers on their own clock, so an early send buys a parallel day. They still go at the TOP of the digest as well.

3) Conclusions are a RECOMMENDATION, not settled law, and my approval here is of scope only - I am not pre-approving your findings. Write it so the operator can pick: where you argue a mechanic should change, give the cost line (which tests in Godot/tests/ move, what save data breaks, what determinism costs) next to the recommendation, and mark anything that depends on an unanswered operator question as blocked-on-Q1/Q2/Q3 rather than deciding it yourself. Kalli K19 owns the visual half in parallel; if your architecture forces a visual consequence, state it as a constraint on K19 and I reconcile the two.

Restating the two hard gates so there is no ambiguity at push time: read every file you cite, and name the specific tests in Godot/tests/ that would have to move for each proposed mechanic change. A change proposed without its test list is not done.
